edges.description: Joints held immobile through development become fixed in flexion.
Reduced fetal finger flexion-extension excursion fixes the interphalangeal joints in flexion.
Intrauterine distal limb hypomobility produces congenital clubfoot deformity.
Diminished fetal mandibular movement impairs mandibular growth, resulting in micrognathia.
Skin and soft tissue across a persistently flexed joint fail to expand, producing a web.
Asymmetric vertebral fusion produces a structural curve that progresses with growth rather than responding to bracing alone.
Extensive thoracic and lumbar vertebral fusions impair longitudinal trunk growth, causing disproportionate short-trunk short stature.

nodes.description: Embryonic myosin persists postnatally in the small cervical and thoracic multifidus muscles attaching to the distal neural arches of the spine (and in fetal/postnatal bone), whereas it is absent from the intervertebral disc annulus fibrosus, nucleus pulposus, and growth-plate chondrocytes. Impaired function of these paraspinal stabilizing muscles is hypothesized to expose intervertebral discs to extraneous mechanical pressure, driving progressive postnatal disc space narrowing and collapse.

nodes.description: Heterozygous pathogenic MYH3 variants in CPSFS1A and autosomal dominant spondylocarpotarsal synostosis perturb embryonic myosin heavy chain either in the globular motor head (e.g., p.Phe645Cys in actin-binding loop 2, p.Ser243del near the ATP-binding pocket with reduced protein stability, p.Thr333Arg) or in the coiled-coil rod/tail domain (e.g., p.Leu900fs9, p.E1015_D1016delinsVNLF, p.Leu1344Pro). On the distal arthrogryposis model, motor-head missense variants alter actin and nucleotide interactions rather than abolishing protein expression, while dominant rod/tail missense, indel, and truncating variants perturb the coiled-coil backbone and downstream paraspinal signaling without touching active-site motor-head residues.
